title: Evidence for Ubiquitous Carbon Grain Destruction in Hot Protostellar Envelopes
question: Search for signatures of carbon grain (refractory organics) destruction in hot protostellar envelopes by comparing hot and warm gas components of oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor organic molecules across 37 high-mass protostars.

what.value: Warm column densities and emitting areas for CH3OH, CH3CN, HNCO, and C2H3CN (measured from 13C or 18O isotopologues)

evidence.quote: We take the warm column densities for the above species from (cite: Nazari2022ALMAGAL), who measure them from the $^{13}$C or $^{18}$O isotopologues of the targeted molecules
We use the CASSIS spectral analysis tool ((cite: Vastel2015)) to fit the spectra assuming the same emitting area that was used in (cite: Nazari2022ALMAGAL) for the warm component.

what.value: Line lists, frequencies, quantum numbers, E_up, and A_ij of considered lines

evidence.quote: The line lists are taken from the Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy (CDMS; (cite: Muller2001); (cite: Muller2005)).
Frequencies, quantum numbers, $E_{\rm up}$ and $A_{\rm ij}$ of the considered lines are given in Tables B.1 and E.7 of (cite: vanGelder2022) and (cite: Nazari2022ALMAGAL).

what.value: Isotope ratio relations as a function of Galactic center distance

evidence.quote: The isotope ratios in that work were calculated from the relations given in (cite: Wilson1994) and (cite: Milam2005) and the distances of the objects from the Galactic center.

recipe.method: Use pre-extracted spectra from the peak pixel of the CH3CN 12_4-11_4 moment zero map as prepared in earlier work.

recipe.goal: Fit hot gas column densities and excitation temperatures
recipe.method: Fit optically thin high-excitation lines (E_up >= 400 K) of main isotopologues of CH3CN, CH3OH, HNCO, and C2H3CN using a fit-by-eye LTE spectral model in CASSIS while ignoring E_up < 400 K lines.
key_parameters: Fixed T_ex = 300 K when highest-E_up temperature-sensitive lines are not detected (and for all C2H3CN fits); omit hot N if T_ex upper limit <= 200 K
assumptions: Thermal excitation conditions (LTE) and optically thin emission for E_up > 400 K lines
Same emitting area as the warm component in Nazari et al. (2022b)

recipe.goal: Compute and compare hot-to-warm total molecule number ratios
recipe.method: Calculate total number of molecules (N_tot = A * N) in the hot and warm components for CH3OH, HNCO, CH3CN, and C2H3CN, and compute the weighted mean and scatter of N_hot / N_warm across the sample.
assumptions: Lines are optically thin so N_tot = A * N is independent of the assumed emitting area.

recipe.goal: Compare observed ratios with an analytical spherical envelope model
recipe.method: Derive analytical expectation for N_hot / N_warm in a power-law spherical protostellar envelope assuming pure ice sublimation at T_sub without additional hot gas-phase chemistry, and compare with observed ratios.
key_parameters: Density power-law index p = -1.5, temperature power-law index q = -0.4, T_hot = 300 K, T_warm = 150 K
assumptions: Spherical envelope with power-law density and temperature profiles, sublimation temperatures <= 100-150 K, and constant abundance X_hot / X_warm = 1 if no hot gas chemistry occurs.

evidence.quote: In contrast, nitrogen-containing, oxygen-poor molecules (CH$_3$CN and C$_2$H$_3$CN) systematically show an enhancement of a factor ${\sim} 5$ in their hot component

evidence.loc: Observational comparison of hot and warm components
evidence.quote: This results in two distinct population of molecules, with at least a ${\sim}0.7$ dex (factor of ${\sim}$5) difference between the mean of the ratios.

answer_key.quantity: Analytical model expectation for N_hot / N_warm without hot gas chemistry (q = -0.4)

evidence.quote: Assuming $T_{\rm hot} = 300$ K and $T_{\rm warm} = 150$ K consistent with the average excitation temperatures of the hot and warm gas for the studied molecules (see Appendix 9), $(T_{i,\rm{hot}}/T_{i,\rm{warm}})^{-3.75} =0.07$.

Therefore, if there is no additional gas phase chemistry in the hot gas (i.e., $X_{i,\rm hot}/X_{i,\rm warm} = 1$), $$\begin{equation} \frac{\mathcal{N}_{i, \rm hot}}{\mathcal{N}_{i, \rm warm}} \sim 0.1. \end{equation}$$
This will change the power of -3.75 to -3.0 and the value of $\mathcal{N}_{i, \rm hot}/\mathcal{N}_{i, \rm warm}$ from 0.07 to 0.13.

answer_key.quantity: Hot-to-warm abundance enhancement (X_hot / X_warm) for oxygen-poor molecules

evidence.quote: This means an enhancement of oxygen-poor species in the hot gas and $X_{i,\rm hot}/X_{i,\rm warm}$ of ${\gtrsim}5$ for these molecules

score_reason: ALMA project code is public, spectral fitting software (CASSIS) and molecular line databases (CDMS) are public, and full per-source hot column densities and temperatures are tabulated. However, data reduction, spectra extraction, warm column densities, and exact line lists are inherited from companion papers, and the fitting relies on a subjective fit-by-eye method.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMAGAL data are public, the 37 targets and targeted molecular transitions are well-defined (with full details in Nazari et al. 2022b), and the main results are concrete numeric column densities, excitation temperatures, and hot-to-warm ratios.
